subject: SignalForge — APAC telemetry subprocessor notification and onboarding request
messages:
From: Sophie Harris <sophie.harris@signalforge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@signalforge.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: SignalForge onboarding as telemetry processor (APAC) / initial inventory

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads-up from our side: SignalForge is planning to activate a provisional telemetry pipeline for our APAC region to improve signal coverage and reduce latency for customers there. The pipeline will send "non-PII" telemetry (metrics, anonymized performance counters, and service-level traces) to our new processing cluster in Singapore.

We expect to route approximately 5–8% of traffic through this path during the pilot (Oct 1 — Dec 31). Per the DPA, we wanted to notify Redwood and provide the initial subprocessor inventory and dataflow for review so you can confirm there are no objections or regulatory constraints. Attached: "signalforge-subprocessor-inventory.csv" and "apac-dataflow-diagram.png". We've also included a short SOC 2 summary as requested previously.

Key asks:
- Confirmation that SignalForge can be added to the subprocessor roster for APAC pilot by 2029-09-20.
- Any mandatory evidence or additional contractual language you require before we proceed (encryption at rest/transit, onshore fallback for specific tenants, supplier attestations).

We can push the pilot window if you need more time — just tell us what would work. Happy to set a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sophie Harris
Head of Integrations, SignalForge
sophie.harris@signalforge.io | +65 9123 4567

Attachment: signalforge-subprocessor-inventory.csv (csv)
Attachment: apac-dataflow-diagram.png (image)
Attachment: signalforge-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Harris <sophie.harris@signalforge.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: SignalForge onboarding as telemetry processor (APAC) / initial inventory

Thanks Sophie — and thanks for the materials. Looping in Kimberly (contracts/procurement) and Rishi (security/compliance) to kick off the internal review.

High-level: we generally allow telemetry processors on a provisional basis for pilots, but there are two immediate points we need confirmation on before we can greenlight:
1) Does the inventory contain any identifiers that could be considered customer data (tenant IDs, user IDs, IP addresses)? You indicated "non-PII" but please confirm definitively.
2) The dataflow diagram shows a cross-border egress to Singapore; for customers with residency requirements we need an onshore fallback and a clear rollback plan if needed.

Kimberly — would procurement require a DPA amendment for a temporary subprocessor addition, or can we cover this under our existing DPA with an addendum? Please advise next steps and timeline.

Rishi — please review the SOC2 summary and the diagram; flag anything we should request (e.g., key management, HSM/KMS, encryption ciphers, retention windows). If we need an evidence package, Sophie, can you share an SOC2 cover letter and the latest audit dates?

Sophie — if you can confirm the two points above and re-send the inventory with any fields redacted that could be considered tenant-level identifiers, that'll speed things up. If it's helpful, we can treat this as a provisional add and require additional evidence before the pilot reaches 10% traffic.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sophie Harris <sophie.harris@signalforge.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: SignalForge onboarding as telemetry processor (APAC) / initial inventory

Thanks Marissa / Sophie. Quick procurement note:

- We typically handle these as a one-page Subprocessor Addendum (SAA) when the subprocessed data is telemetry/non-PII. The SAA covers the scope, data categories, retention, and termination rights.
- For any cross-border movement, legal may require a signed addendum referencing our standard transfer safeguard language (particularly for EU customers; APAC asks vary by customer).
- If SignalForge is requesting a limited pilot (Oct–Dec) and agrees to the SAA language, we can target approval by 2029-09-20, provided Rishi signs off on the evidence package.

Sophie — can you confirm you are willing to sign our standard SAA (I can share a template) and confirm there are no planned tenant-level identifiers? Also confirm the point of contact for contract signing.

Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Harris <sophie.harris@signalforge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Sep 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: SignalForge onboarding as telemetry processor (APAC) / initial inventory

Sophie — quick technical follow-up after I reviewed the SOC2 summary and diagram. Overall looks reasonable for a telemetry pilot, but please address the following items before we finalize the provisional addendum: 

1) Encryption: confirm TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest. Specify KMS provider and whether keys are customer-segregated or shared.
2) Retention and purge: state the maximum retention for telemetry payloads (we typically request <=90 days unless otherwise agreed).
3) Access controls & logs: provide the log retention for admin access and a contact for emergency access requests.
4) Onshore fallback: outline the rollback plan that allows us to stop routing traffic to Singapore within 24 hours for any tenant on request.

If you can provide a brief cover letter that explicitly confirms (1) no tenant-level identifiers are present, (2) the answers to the four items above, and (3) the latest SOC2 audit date, we can proceed with the SAA and target the 2029-09-20 approval.

If any of the items are a blocker (e.g., shared keys rather than dedicated KMS), flag that now and we can discuss mitigations (escrow, onshore processing, or limiting traffic).

Thanks — Rishi.
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
